Use a subprocess only when the description gives a multi-step phase with its own internal steps, and keep the action that initiates that phase as a separate task before it. Model the phase's final state as the end of the flow only when the description states it as the process outcome.

When the description opens with an activity that an actor performs (for example, recording, collecting or preparing something) before any other step, and the process start is not itself an external message, signal, time or condition: Model the opening activity as a task placed directly after a plain start event, labeled with a verb-object name taken from the description, and connect it in sequence to the next step. Do not move the activity into the start event's label, and do not omit it because the start event already names its result.

When the description says a process begins when a participant performs an action through one of several alternative channels (for example online or by phone), with each channel named as a separate way of performing that action: Model the start as a start event with no action label, followed by one task per alternative channel, each labelled with the action performed through that channel. Merge the channel tasks with an exclusive gateway, placed before the first step that follows the action. Do not collapse the channels into a single task or into the start event.

result.rule: Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
